questions.question: Who among the following freedom fighters is known as 'Deshbandhu'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittaranjan Das**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Chittaranjan Das was a prominent Indian freedom fighter and political leader known as 'Deshbandhu', which means 'Friend of the Nation'.
 
• He played a significant role in the Non-Cooperation Movement against British rule in India.
 
• Chittaranjan Das was the founder of the Swaraj Party along with Motilal Nehru, which aimed at attaining self-governance within the British Empire.
 
• He was also a renowned lawyer and defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the Alipore Bomb Case, further establishing his reputation as a key figure in the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Cooperation Movement**

 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920, it was a significant phase of the Indian independence movement aimed at resisting British rule through nonviolent means.
 
• The movement saw widespread participation across India with actions like boycotting British goods, institutions, and services.
 
• Chittaranjan Das played a crucial role in galvanizing support for the movement, especially in Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Swaraj Party**
 
 
• Founded by Chittaranjan Das and Motilal Nehru in 1923, the Swaraj Party aimed to achieve self-governance within the British Empire.
 
• The party sought to enter legislative councils through elections to obstruct and eventually end British rule from within the system.
 
• This was a strategic shift from Gandhi's non-cooperation approach and aimed at more direct political engagement.
 
 
 
• **Alipore Bomb Case**
 
 
• In 1908, Aurobindo Ghosh and several others were arrested for their alleged involvement in a conspiracy to bomb a British magistrate's carriage.
 
• Chittaranjan Das defended Aurobindo Ghosh, and his eloquent defense played a significant role in the acquittal of Ghosh.
 
• This case was a landmark in the Indian legal history and highlighted the role of Indian lawyers in the freedom movement.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress**
 
 
• Established in 1885, the Indian National Congress (INC) was the principal leader of the Indian independence movement.
 
• Chittaranjan Das was an active member of the INC and held significant positions, including the President of the Gaya session in 1922.
 
• His contributions to the INC were vital in shaping the strategies and policies of the freedom struggle during the early 20th century.

questions.question: In which of the following years was VD Savarkar sent to Andaman Jail by the British?

__
 
• Vinayak Damodar Savarkar, also known as Veer Savarkar, was a prominent freedom fighter, social reformer, and writer.
 
• In 1910, Savarkar was arrested by the British for his involvement in revolutionary activities against the colonial regime.
 
• He was subsequently tried and sentenced to two life terms of imprisonment totaling fifty years and was deported to the Andaman Islands in 1911.
 
• The Cellular Jail in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, also known as Kala Pani, was where he was imprisoned. This jail was notorious for its harsh conditions and was used by the British to exile political prisoners.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar:**

 
 
• He was born on May 28, 1883, in Bhagur, a village near Nashik in Maharashtra, India.
 
• He was a staunch advocate of Hindutva and is credited with founding the ideology.
 
• Savarkar wrote several books, including "The First War of Indian Independence 1857," which presented the uprising of 1857 as a unified and national effort against British rule.
 
• After his release from prison, he continued his activities as a social reformer and political activist, although he was kept under strict surveillance by the British authorities.
 
 
 
• **Cellular Jail (Kala Pani):**
 
 
• The Cellular Jail is located in Port Blair, the capital of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• It was constructed by the British between 1896 and 1906 to exile political prisoners.
 
• The jail is known for its solitary confinement cells, which were designed to isolate prisoners from each other and prevent them from communicating.
 
• Many prominent Indian freedom fighters, including Batukeshwar Dutt, Yogendra Shukla, and more, were imprisoned here.
 
• Today, the Cellular Jail is a national memorial monument.

questions.question: In 1936, The Independent Labour Party was founded by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BR Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dr. BR Ambedkar was a prominent Indian jurist, economist, and social reformer who campaigned against social discrimination towards the untouchables (Dalits).
 
• He was the principal architect of the Constitution of India and served as the first Law Minister of India.
 
• In 1936, Dr. BR Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party, which aimed to secure social justice and eradicate social inequalities.
 
• The party contested the Bombay Legislative Assembly elections held in 1937 and won 15 seats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Independent Labour Party (ILP)**

 
 
• The Independent Labour Party was established by BR Ambedkar on 15 August 1936 in Bombay.
 
• The ILP was formed to address the issues faced by the working class and the marginalized sections of society, particularly the Dalits.
 
• The party's manifesto emphasized the need for state socialism in the sphere of industry and agriculture.
 
• It also advocated for labor rights, including fair wages, decent working conditions, and social security measures for workers.
 
 
 
• **BR Ambedkar**
 
 
• Born on 14 April 1891, Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was a prolific scholar and an influential leader of the Dalit community in India.
 
• He played a crucial role in drafting the Indian Constitution and was a strong advocate for the rights of the oppressed and marginalized.
 
• Ambedkar's efforts led to significant social reforms, including the abolition of untouchability and the promotion of education and employment opportunities for Dalits.
 
• He embraced Buddhism in 1956 along with many of his followers, which marked a significant movement in the Dalit community towards religious and social empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform Movements in India**
 
 
• Social reform movements in India aimed at eradicating social evils and injustices prevalent in society, such as caste discrimination, gender inequality, and child marriage.
 
• Prominent social reformers included Raja Ram Mohan Roy, who worked towards the abolition of Sati, and Jyotirao Phule, who fought for the rights of the lower castes and women's education.
 
• These movements laid the foundation for a more equitable and just society in India by challenging traditional norms and advocating for progressive changes.
 
• The contributions of leaders like BR Ambedkar were instrumental in shaping modern India's social and political landscape.

questions.question: ‘Drain of Wealth’, a critique of the colonial exploitation, was given by which of the following nationalist leaders?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji, also known as the "Grand Old Man of India", was an early Indian political leader, merchant, scholar, and writer.
 
• He is best known for his work in the Indian National Congress and his influential economic writings on the drain theory, which criticized British economic policies in India.
 
• In his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India", he detailed how the British were draining India of its wealth.
 
• Naoroji's economic analysis and advocacy laid the groundwork for Indian economic nationalism and inspired future leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drain of Wealth Theory**

 
 
• The "Drain of Wealth" theory proposed by Dadabhai Naoroji argued that Britain was systematically transferring Indian wealth to Britain.
 
• Naoroji highlighted that a significant portion of India's wealth and resources were being drained to Britain without any adequate economic or material returns to India.
 
• This theory was primarily articulated through his writings and speeches, particularly in his seminal work "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India".
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**
 
 
• Founded in 1885, the Indian National Congress was one of the first political movements to demand greater autonomy and self-governance for India.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji was one of the founding members and served as the President of the INC three times.
 
• The INC played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement, advocating for civil rights, representation, and eventually complete independence from British rule.
 
 
 
• **Economic Nationalism**
 
 
• Economic nationalism is a body of policies that emphasize domestic control of the economy, labor, and capital formation, often advocating protectionism and import substitution.
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji's critique of British economic policies laid the foundation for economic nationalism in India, influencing the Swadeshi movement and later economic policies post-independence.

• He also established **Fergusson College in Pune**.

• **Kesari and Mahratta** were the two newspapers started by; Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

• Along with Bipin Chandra Pal and Bal Gangadhar Tilak, he formed the Lal-Bal-Pal trio of extremist leaders.
 
• He Fought against **untouchability**.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai Founded the** Servants of People Society in 1921**.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai Founded **Arya Gazette**.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai founded the **Home Rule League of America in 1917 in New York**.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi(1869-1948)**.
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi, by name of Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, (was born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, India.**
 
• Mahatma Gandhi was an Indian **lawyer, politician, social activist, and writer** who became the leader of the nationalist movement against the British rule of India. 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi came to be considered the** father of India**.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi was known for his** non-violence protest **and was a leading figure in freedom movements.

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers established Satyashodhak Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jyotirao Phule**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj** (Truth-seeker's Society) was a social reform society founded by **Jyotirao Phule** in Pune, Maharashtra, on **24 September 1873**.
 
• It espoused **a mission of education and increased social rights and political access for underprivileged groups, focused especially on women, Shudras, and Dalits**, in Maharashtra.
 
• Satya Shodhak Samaj refused to regard the Vedas as sacrosanct, opposed idol worship, denounced the Chaturvarnya System (the caste system), and rejected the need for a Brahman priestly class as educational and religious leaders.
 
• The existence of God was replaced by **Nirmik**.
 
• **Deenbandhu** was the name of the mouthpiece of the Satya Shodhak Samaj.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Jyotirao Phule:

__
 
• He was born on 11 April 1827 in Katgun, Satara District in Maharashtra.
 
• He belonged to the Mali caste of gardeners.
 
• It was in 1848 that he read American political activist and philosopher’s work** ‘Rights of Man’,** this book influenced his idea of social justice.
 
• He is credited with using the word **‘Dalit’** for the depressed classes for the first time.
 
• It is a **Marathi word meaning ‘broken’ or ‘crushed’.**
 
• Phule inspired many latter-day leaders including B R Ambedkar.
 
• Phule was also the Commissioner of the Poona Municipality from 1876 till 1883.

questions.question: Who was the political guru of Subhash Chandra Bose?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chittaranjan Das**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chittaranjan Das** was the political mentor of Subhash Chandra Bose.
 
• Chittaranjan Das was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement and an advocate for self-governance.
 
• He played a significant role in Bose's early political career and was instrumental in shaping his nationalist ideas.
 
• Das founded the Swaraj Party in 1923 along with Motilal Nehru to express the discontent with the policies of the British government.
 
• Subhash Chandra Bose admired Das for his dedication to the cause of Indian independence and considered him a guiding force in his own political journey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose** was a prominent leader in the Indian independence movement known for his radical approach and leadership of the Indian National Army (INA).
 
• He was a key figure in the struggle against British colonial rule and sought to achieve independence through armed struggle.
 
• Bose's famous slogan was "**Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!**"
 
• He formed the **Azad Hind Government** in exile during World War II and sought support from Axis powers to fight against the British.
 
• Despite his controversial alliances, Bose remains a revered figure in Indian history for his dedication and sacrifices for the nation's independence.

questions.question: Who among the following persuaded Mahatma Gandhi to allow women to join the Salt Satyagraha movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay **was an **Indian social reformer** and **freedom activist.**
 
• One of the women who is credited with **convincing Gandhiji** to allow **women's involvement **in the **Salt Satyagraha movement **was Kamaladevi.
 
• She was a member of the **seven-person leadership team** in the renowned **Salt Satyagraha (1930).**
 
• The team was tasked with preparing salt on the **Bombay beachfront.**
 
• **Avantikabai Gokhale** was the only other woman on the team who volunteered.
 
• She received the **Sangeet Natak Academy Fellowship** in** 1974.**
 
• The Indian government awarded her the** Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan** in **1955 and 1987**, respectively.
 
• Because of her contributions to the handloom industry, she is known as **Hatkargha Maa**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Annie Besant:**

 
 
• British socialist Annie Besant was also an **advocate** for **women's rights, home rule, and theosophy.**
 
• She was a** fierce advocate **for both** Irish and Indian independence.**
 
• For** fifteen years,** Besant actively promoted **scientific materialism **and **atheism in England.**
 
 
 
• **Ashalata Sen:**
 
 
• Ashalata Sen was a prominent member of the** Indian independence struggle** as well as an** activist, poet, and social worker.**
 
 
 
• **Ambabai:**
 
 
• Ambabai was a native of **Karnataka.**
 
• She was** twelve** when she **got married** and **sixteen** when she** lost her husband.**
